implementation.description: 'native' marks a device implemented as a Rust module in the core. Its commands carry no wire behaviour.

reason.description: Required when implementation is 'native': why the protocol cannot be expressed as data.

label.description: A short name for a person: what a form or button shows ("Channel", "Frequency").

description.description: One plain sentence on what the value means, its unit and numbering, for a person choosing it.

oneOf.description: A step with conditions. when_set: sent only when the named setting is non-empty, decided from configuration before connecting. after_prompt: sent only once the device has sent this text (line-tcp). refused: a reply line matching this regex is the device refusing the credential. accepted: once a reply line matches this regex, refused stops applying.

after_prompt.description: line-tcp only. Literal text the device sends before this step is accepted, such as a password prompt with no line ending. Nothing is sent, and the device is not reported connected, until it arrives; without it within the timeout the connection is dropped and retried.

refused.description: Regex over reply lines. A match is the device refusing the credential: terminal, never retried.

await_reply.description: On a transport whose device replies: queue the step like a query, so its reply is consumed and no command goes ahead of it.

accepted.description: With refused: regex over reply lines. Once a line matches, the device has accepted the login and refused no longer applies.

models.description: The model ids this message is for; it is skipped for any other model (SPEC.md §4, Messages per model).

codes.description: Device-wide map of numeric response code to failure message, used with expect.code_range.

conversions.description: Named piecewise-linear conversions between a wire value and the value an operator uses (a fader law). Used in templates as {x:to.<name>} (value to wire) and {x:from.<name>} (wire to value), and by expect.convert (SPEC.md §4).

points.description: [wire, value] pairs joined by straight lines; wire strictly rising, value strictly rising or strictly falling. Values outside the points do not convert.

maps.description: Named value tables: a parameter's plain text (an enum value, true or false, a decimal integer) to the wire text, used in templates as {x:map.<name>}. A value the table does not list is rejected before transmission (SPEC.md §4, Value tables).

streams.description: Continuous media a native module publishes, such as a camera's live view, keyed by stream name. Consumers watch a stream by name; frames are delivered outside the event queue, newest only. See SPEC.md, Native modules, Streams.

format.description: The encoding of every frame: jpeg is one complete JPEG image (ITU-T T.81) per frame.

models.description: The models that have the stream; every model when absent.

state.description: Telemetry fields the device reports, keyed by dotted path; '*' stands for a channel number.

telemetry.description: How the device's own messages become state (SPEC.md §8).

every_ms.description: Sent again at this interval (a subscription that expires, or a poll).
Sent again at this interval (a subscription that expires, or a poll).

match.description: Regex over the whole message; captures are {1}, {2}, ...

header.description: Regex over a block's first line.

each_line.description: With header: regex applied to every following line.

fields.description: With header: 'name: value' lines to state paths.

address.description: Regex over an OSC address; arguments are {arg0}, {arg1}, ...

json_arg.description: With address and json: the string argument holding JSON (default 0).

oneOf.description: Value template over the rule's captures.

map.description: Wire text to state value; wire values not listed are not assigned.

oneOf.description: Remove the path from state: a declared value, or a whole subtree of declared values (a JSON merge patch null).

state.description: State path template to value, or to {delete: true} to remove it.

path.description: Regex over an HTTP request's path and query; the rule handles its reply.

json.description: With path: names for values taken from a JSON reply, by JSON path. With address: from the JSON in the string argument at json_arg. With json_match alone: from the JSON message.

headers.description: With path: names for response header values, by header name in any case (SPEC.md §8).

xml_each.description: With path: an XML element name; each such element in the reply is a match, its attributes the captures.

json_each.description: With path or json_match, and json: a JSON path to an array; the rule matches once per element, json paths relative to it.

arg_types.description: With address: the message's OSC type tags must be exactly these (without the comma), for a device that sends different shapes on one address.

json_match.description: JSON path to an RE2-safe regex its value must match (a string as is, anything else as compact JSON). Alone: a JSON message on a websocket, an event stream, or a line of a line transport. With path: the JSON reply must match too. Captures are {1}, {2}, ... across the regexes in order, after the path's.

request_match.description: With path: JSON path to an RE2-safe regex the JSON body of the request the reply answers must match, so replies sharing one path (JSON-RPC) can be told apart. Its captures come after the path's and before json_match's.

websocket.description: A websocket opened beside the transport, for a device that takes commands one way (REST) and pushes state on a websocket. Its messages go through the update rules; it is reopened with backoff when it closes.

scheme.description: ws or wss, or {setting: name} naming an enum setting whose values are ws and wss.

accept_invalid_certs.description: Over wss, accept a certificate that does not chain to a trusted root, such as a device's self-signed one. The connection is encrypted; the device is not authenticated. Defaults to the http transport's accept_invalid_certs.

send.description: Text messages (templates over settings) sent each time the websocket opens: the subscriptions.

every_ms.description: Send the send items again at this interval while the websocket is open: a keepalive the device requires, or a request it answers with state.

socketio.description: The websocket speaks Socket.IO over Engine.IO (path usually /socket.io/): the core adds EIO and transport to the query, joins the namespace when the server opens, answers pings, sends each send item as an event (a JSON array, ["name", data]), and gives each event to the json_match rules as {"event", "data", "args"}.

engine_io.description: 4 for Socket.IO 3 and 4 (the server pings), 3 for Socket.IO 2 (the client pings).

auth.description: A JSON object, a template over settings, sent with the namespace connect as Socket.IO's handshake auth (FreeShow's {"token": ...}).

sse.description: A server-sent event stream opened beside an http transport, with the transport's credential, for a device that pushes changes as text/event-stream. Each event goes to the json_match rules as {"event": name, "data": data} (data parsed where it is JSON) and its data to the text rules; it is reopened with backoff when it closes.

extension.description: A native addition to a spec-driven device, for what the format cannot express. Named here so it is never hidden.

ports.description: Every port the integration uses, with its default. Exactly the ports the core really uses: the control port (OpenRequest.port overrides it), and any push, feedback, notification or discovery ports. port null means there is no default and one must be given.

setting.description: The setting that changes this port.

when.description: When it applies, if not always: a setting's value or a model.

reply_framing.description: How a reply is delimited. Defaults to 'block' for framing: block, otherwise 'line'. 'terminated' ends a message at any of reply_terminators, with no line ending needed.

reply_terminators.description: With reply_framing: terminated. A message runs up to and including the first of these; surrounding spaces and line endings are dropped.

reply_match.description: RE2-safe regex. A message matching it is a command reply; any other message is unsolicited.

error_match.description: RE2-safe regex for the device's error answer, which names nothing it answers (Shure's < REP ERR >): it is taken as the reply of a command waiting with expect.reply_contains.

reply_match.description: RE2-safe regex. A datagram matching it is a command reply; any other is unsolicited.

listen_port.description: Receive on this fixed local port, shared between devices and routed by source address, for devices that send to a configured destination. A port, or {setting: name} naming an integer setting; an empty setting means no fixed port.

https_port.description: With scheme {setting: name}: the default port when the setting chooses https (Magewell: 80, or 443).

scheme.description: http or https, or {setting: name} naming an enum setting whose values are http and https, for devices the operator can switch.

refusal_status.description: HTTP statuses that mean the credential was refused, for devices that use 403 for other errors.

accept_invalid_certs.description: Over HTTPS, accept a certificate that does not chain to a trusted root, such as a device's self-signed one. The connection is encrypted; the device is not authenticated.

refusal_json.description: JSON paths to regexes: an error answer (4xx or 5xx) whose JSON body matches every one is a refusal of the credential too, whatever its status, for a service that names a refused token in its error body (the Graph API's error.code 190 under HTTP 400).

auth.description: The credential sent: a method, or {setting: name} naming an enum setting whose values are methods, for a service taking more than one kind of credential.

headers.description: Headers sent on every request, the push websocket's opening and the event stream: each header name maps to a template over settings ({settings.name}). A header that renders empty is not sent. Authorization, Content-Type and Host are set by the core and may not be named (Twitch's Client-Id: '{settings.client_id}').

auth_header.description: With auth: header, the header the token setting is sent in, as is (mimoLive's X-MimoLive-Password-SHA256). Nothing is sent while the token is empty.

oauth.description: With auth: oauth2, where and how the access_token setting is refreshed with the refresh_token setting (RFC 6749 section 6). The token_url setting, when set, replaces token_url.

token_url.description: The service's token endpoint, an absolute https URL.

refresh_ahead_s.description: Refresh this many seconds before the access token expires (at half its life for a token living shorter than twice this).

client_auth.description: How the client authenticates to the token endpoint: client_id and client_secret (when set) in the form body, or HTTP Basic.

validate.description: A token validation endpoint the service requires the application to call (Twitch: on start and hourly). The core sends the access token there once the device opens and after each refresh, then every every_s while open, whether or not it is monitored. A 401 refreshes the token and validates the new one when there is a refresh token; otherwise, or when the new token is refused too, it is the terminal unauthorized.

url.description: The validation endpoint, an absolute https URL, on any host.

every_s.description: Seconds between validations while the device is open.

scheme.description: The Authorization scheme the access token is sent with (Twitch documents OAuth).

probe.description: Liveness check, any answer meaning reachable: one request, or a list of requests each naming its models, the first for the device's model used.

session.description: A login whose answer carries a session (a cookie or a header) sent back on every later request; renewed when the device says it ended (SPEC.md §2, Sessions).

login.description: The login request (templates over settings), or a list of them each naming its models.

capture.description: What of the login's answer is the session: {cookie: name} the named Set-Cookie, or every one with "*" (the default), sent back as Cookie; {header: name} a response header, sent back in a header of that name.

relogin.description: An answer to any request meaning the session ended: the core logs in again and sends that request once more.

refused.description: An answer to the login refusing the credential: terminal, as any refusal.

scheme.description: ws or wss, or {setting: name} naming an enum setting whose values are ws and wss.

accept_invalid_certs.description: Over wss, accept a certificate that does not chain to a trusted root, such as a device's self-signed one. The connection is encrypted; the device is not authenticated.

auth.description: Credential on the opening request, from the username and password, or token, settings. A 401 or 403 answer is terminal, as for http.

reply_match.description: RE2-safe regex. For replies taken in order: a message not matching it is never taken as a reply.

supports.description: Allow-list of command keys. A command absent here MUST be refused for this model.

command.description: 'send' is required for spec-driven devices and forbidden for native ones; tools/validate.py enforces this.

oneOf.description: Ordered sequence; all messages must succeed.

label.description: A short name for a person: what a form or button shows ("Channel", "Frequency").

description.description: One plain sentence on what the value means, its unit and numbering, for a person choosing it.

models.description: The model ids this message is for; it is skipped for any other model (SPEC.md §4, Messages per model).

reply_address.description: Telemetry poll only: RE2-safe regex over the address the device answers on, for a query answered on another address (ETC Eos: /eos/get/... on /eos/out/get/...).

models.description: The model ids this message is for; it is skipped for any other model (SPEC.md §4, Messages per model).

raw_query.description: Sent verbatim, never re-encoded. For positional CGI arguments.

models.description: The model ids this message is for; it is skipped for any other model (SPEC.md §4, Messages per model).

session.description: false: sent without the session of transport.session, and needing none, so it does not log in first (a ping).

matches.description: RE2-safe regex; capture group 1 is the returned value.

json_path.description: JSON path into the reply: the HTTP body, or for OSC the string argument at arg.

json_equals.description: JSON path to the value it must hold, in the same JSON as json_path; any other value fails the command.

header.description: HTTP only. A response header whose value is returned (a Location, an ETag); the command fails without it.

code_range.description: Inclusive success range for a leading numeric response code.

code_path.description: JSON path to the reply's numeric status code, used in place of a leading code by code_range and codes (Magewell's $.status).

address.description: OSC only. Templated address the reply must carry.

arg.description: OSC only. Index of the reply argument returned as the value.

reply_json.description: Websocket only. JSON path to a template: the reply is the message whose values at these paths equal the rendered templates (a request id, or the parameter asked for). Without it, the next message is the reply.

reply_contains.description: Line transports only. A template: the reply is the first message holding the rendered text (the parameter and channel asked about); other messages arriving meanwhile are not the reply. Without it, the next message is the reply.

convert.description: The name of a conversion: the returned value is converted from the wire.

models.description: Model ids, or the single entry 'all'.

json.description: JSON paths to RE2-safe regexes the answer's body must all match.
